oci.title: New OCI, adult naturalised non-US national
oci.chunk_text:
NEW OCI Checklist - For ADULT (NON-US National By Naturalization) > IMPORTANT GUIDELINES

 IT IS ABSOLUTELY MANDATORY to complete VFS ONLINE REGISTRATION PROCESS before sending your physical application. Failure to complete online registration process will result in returning your application unprocessed.  All the photocopies of the documents that are being submitted must be in full page and clearly legible. Photos should be visible and other information should be clearly readable.  Please do not send original documents unless specified. VFS will not be responsible for return of any additional original documents submitted  Please ensure that all data entries provided in your application match with your existing passport. If not, please provide the supporting documentation.  Please select the correct Indian mission based on the place where you reside in the USA and the mission’s jurisdiction. Mission jurisdiction can be viewed at h t t p : / / v i s a . v f s g l o b a l . c o m / u s a / e n / i n d / a t t e n d - c e n t r e  You are recommended to fill a fresh OCI application form if your form has been completed more than 70 days ago. This might help avoid any processing delays in case your form expires at 90 days before submission to the Mission’  After submission online, no changes can be made. In case of an error, please fill a new online application form.  If your application lacks any of the documents listed in this checklist, your application will be put “on Hold” and an email notification highlighting the deficiencies will be sent to you. You must complete application within 7 days from the date of receipt of the email notification. Post receipt of missing documents, VFS India Consular application Centre will update the system in 48 – 72 business hours hence track the status only after 48-72 hours.  Envelope should be superscribed as “NEW OCI - MINOR. One Envelope can contain only one application only. DON’T STAPLE THE DOCUMENTS Please note:  VFS INDIA CONSULAR APPLICATION CENTRE employees cannot edit or make any changes to your online application form.  THE CONSULATE RESERVES THE RIGHT TO CALL FOR ADDITIONAL DOCUMENTS, AS CONSIDERED NECESSARY.  YOUR APPLICATION STATUS WILL BE UPDATED IN 48 – 72 HOURS POST ITS DELIVERY TO THE VFS INDIA CONSULAR APPLICATION CENTRE. TO TRACK THE STATUS ONLINE, CLICK HERE

oci.chunk_text:
citizenship by way of naturalization/registration: > S. No DOCUMENTS

1. Duly signed OCI Application Form in original. The application may be submitted online on the Government of India’s official website https://ociservices.gov.in and physical copy of the OCI application needs to be submitted with supporting documents. Please read the following carefully:
• If you are applying for OCI card for the first time and you never held PIO card, kindly apply for new OCI registration.
• If you are already an OCI Cardholder, kindly use OCI
• If you are a PIO Cardholder, kindly register through OCI Registration (In Lieu Of Valid PIO-Card).
• If you are a PIO Cardholder and card is in lost state, kindly register through OCI Registration (In Lieu Of Lost PIO -Card).
• To reprint your already registered application, kindly use 'Re- Print Submitted Application' service. In case of urgent travel, applicants may apply for appropriate visa.
2. Photograph & Signature: For detailed specifications - please click here
• The physical photo must be affixed on the physical application form and the digital photo must be uploaded on the OCI form online. Physical and uploaded photograph must be identical.
• The digital signature must also be uploaded online on the OCI portal (only in blue or black ink). Uploaded signature must match with the signature on the physical application form and passport.

3. Parental Authorization Form (Notarized and Original): Both parents must sign the parental authorization form, which should be duly notarized. Signatures of the parents on OCI Application Form, their passports/ID proofs and parental authorization form must be identical. Click here for the Form Mismatch of signatures will result in delay in processing the OCI application, which is also liable to be rejected Note: One parent may sign the Parental Authorization Form only in the following conditions:
• If parents are divorced and only one parent has legal custody of the minor applicant (and the other parent has no visitation rights or paying child support), court order regarding the legal custody must be provided. If the court order is in any foreign language other than English, translation in English by authorized translator is to be enclosed.
• If one parent is not alive, copy of the death certificate must be provided.
• If the parent is single adoptive parent, copy of adoption document must be provided.
4. Copy of current valid passport with validity of minimum 6 months at the time of submission of application. Information page of the passport should be duly signed at the designated space. The document must be self-attested.
5. Copy of last held Indian passport (first 2 and last 2 pages). The document must be self-attested.
6. Undertaking for Surrender of Indian Voter Card and Ration Card – Mandatory for all prior Indian Citizens (Click here for the format)

7. Copy of the Naturalization Certificate (the document must be self - attested): The naturalization certificate should be duly signed at the designated space. If the applicant has acquired naturalization through parents and the applicant doesn’t possess separate naturalization certificate, a notarized affidavit signed by both parents may be submitted along with copies of their naturalization certificates (Click here for the format).

9. Name Change Document issued by the local court or a duly notarized affidavit regarding change in name, if the current legal name as per current foreign passport is different from the name given in the last held Indian passport. Previous name as per last held Indian passport must invariably be mentioned in the OCI application, failing which the OCI application is liable to be rejected. To be more specific, previous name must be mentioned even in case of minor variation, including variation of a single letter. The following examples may help: Example 1: If a person’s name as per last held Indian passport is TRIPTA TIWARI and the name as per foreign passport is TRIPTA TYAGI (surname changed after marriage), previous name as per last held Indian passport must be mentioned as TRIPTA TIWARI in the relevant column of the online OCI application. Example 2: If a person’s name as per last held Indian passport is HARISH CHANDER GUPTA and the name as per foreign passport is HARISH C. GUPTA, previous name as per last held Indian passport must be mentioned as HARISH CHANDER GUPTA in the relevant column of the online OCI application. Example 3: If a person’s name as per last held Indian passport is GIRDHAR PRAKASH and the name as per foreign passport is GIRI DHAR PRAKASH (one more ‘i’ in the first name), previous name as per last held Indian passport must be mentioned as GIRDHAR PRAKASH in the relevant column of the online OCI application. Example 4: If a person’s name as per last held Indian passport is CHARU LATA and the name as per foreign passport is LATA CHARU, previous name as per last held Indian passport must be mentioned as CHARU LATA

in the relevant column of the online OCI application. Example 5: If a person’s name as per last held Indian passport is GHANSHYAMBHAI PATEL and the name as per foreign passport is GHANSHYAM PATEL, previous name as per last held Indian passport must be mentioned as GHANSHYAMBHAI PATEL in the relevant column of the online OCI application. Note : Date of birth in the current foreign passport must match with the date of birth mentioned in the last held Indian passport. Mismatch is not acceptable, and the application is liable to be rejected.
10. Marriage Certificate of Parents: If the marriage is solemnized in India, Marriage Certificate issued by Marriage Registrar is required. Marriage Certificate issued by any religious body is not acceptable. If parents are divorced, copy of the divorce decree may be provided. If one parent is not alive, copy of the death certificate may be provided. (The document must be self -attested). If your marriage certificate or divorce decree was issued outside India, it must be apostilled or attested by the respective foreign authority or government. For example, if your document was issued in the United States, you must contact the County Office or Municipality Office in the same state or city where the certificate was issued to get it apostilled. Please do not send original apostilled documents to VFS or Consulate office. We required self-attested copies of apostilled documents.
11. Copies of current passports of the parents – If parents are holding Indian passport, please provide first two and last pages of the Indian passport copies.

12. PROOF OF LEGAL STATUS OF PARENTS IN THE USA (IF HOLDING NON- USA PASSPORT) (The document must be self-attested). Pleas e submit any one of the following documents:
• Copy of valid Green Card – Front and Back, OR
• Copy of valid EAD – Front and Back, OR
• Copy of valid long-term US visa, OR
• In case vis a extension is pending, I-797A Approval Notice / I-797C Receipt Notice along with recently expired visa may be submitted.
13. Copies of OCI cards issued to parents, if ever obtained and available. (The document must be self-attested).
14. Copy of Indian visa, if ever obtained and available (The document must be self- attested).
15. Proof of address (the document must be self-attested): Proof of address must match with the present address as per application. Copy of any one of the following documents may be provided as proof of address:
• State issued Identity Card, OR
• Driving license, OR
• Utility bill – water / gas / electricity / telephone (Latest one, not more than 3-month-old), OR
• Valid Lease Agreement, OR
• Mortgage, OR
• Income Tax Return, OR
• For college/university students living in university housing/dormitories, a letter from the institution on official letterhead giving details of the applicant’s present address, OR
• In case of applicant residing with parents / children / relatives, a notarized undertaking from them with any copy of address proof as indicated above. Note:
• Expired documents like lease/driving license are not acceptable as valid proof of address.
• PO Box number is not acceptable as valid proof of address.
• Copy of Driver’s License should not be cut down to smaller size.

The responsibility lies primarily with the applicant to fill in correct details in the OCI application. Also, that some details as per the OCI application are not editable subsequently. In some cases, the OCI application with errors is liable to be rejected and may be returned to the applicant for submitting fresh OCI application with correct details.

3. Indian Embassy / Consulate reserves the right to ask for additional documents for
processing the OCI application. Embassy/Consulate is under no obligation to inform reasons, if the OCI application is rejected and the decision of the Embassy/Consulate will be final. COMMON MISTAKES IN OCI APPLICATIONS RESULTING IN REJECTION
1. Poor quality of uploaded photo / signature. Please ensure to upload good quality photo and signature as per prescribed specifications.
2. All supporting documents not uploaded online.
3. Incorrect passport number / date of issue of passport
4. Incorrect name / place of birth / date of birth
5. Full names of parents / spouse not mentioned or not matching with their current legal names.
6. Marital status / spouse name not mentioned.
7. Incorrect contact numbers and email address.
8. Part-B of OCI application not signed / Part -B (Minor Child) not signed by any of the parents.
9. Previous name not mentioned (if there is change of name, kindly mention the sam e in relevant column of the application and provide supporting documents).
10. Incomplete postal address (please provide complete address ZIP code in the application).
11. Proof of native address not provided (proof of native address must be provided if application is being submitted in a country of residence other than home country). USEFUL TIPS FOR FILLING OCI APPLICATION ONLINE

oci.title: Foreign national previously holding Indian passport, minor

1. Please ensure that you have all the supporting documents in pdf and photo/signature in JPEG format as per specifications before starting online application.
2. Fill all the details in the application very carefully and exactly as per documents. Please ensure that all the details like full names, date of birth, place of birth are exactly as per current passport. Please note that the date of birth, if different from the one mentioned in the last held Indian passport, is not acceptable.
3. Upload all the supporting documents under their correct category / equivalent category (e.g. Birth Certificate can be uploaded under Relationship category). If you are unable to find suitable category to upload the document, please upload all the remaining documents (including any legal document) under current passport category along with current passport. MOST IMPORTANT IS TO UPLOAD ALL THE SUPPORTING DOCUMENTS.
4. Kindly check all the details of the OCI application once printed. In case photo/signature and documents are not uploaded properly, these can be uploaded easily by selecting appropriate option (Re-upload image/upload/re- upload documents) available on the website. Please note that the file reference number required to re-upload photo/signature/documents is written vertically on left side and also below the bar code at the bottom of first page of application form submitted online.
5. In case any information is wrong, please fill the form again.

6. PROOF OF LEGAL STATUS IN THE USA (IF HOLDING NON-USA PASSPORT) 1
(The document must be self-attested). Pleas e submit any one of the following documents:
• Copy of valid Green Card – Front and Back, OR
• Copy of valid EAD – Front and Back, OR
• Copy of valid long-term US visa, OR
• In case vis a extension is pending, I-797A Approval Notice / I-797C Receipt Notice along with recently expired visa may be submitted.
7. Copy of Employment / Work Letter – applicable in case of adult applicant (the docum ent must be self-attested) :
• If applicant is employed, a letter from the employer describing job profile of the applicant may be provided.
• If applicant is self-employed / doing business, some documentary proof of self-employment/business may be provided.
• If applicant is retired, some documentary proof regarding retirement and details of the last employer may be provided.
• If applicant is a student, some documentary proof, e. g. admission letter, may be provided.
• If applicant has never been employed/self-employed, a written statement may be submitted.

Signatures of the parents on OCI Application Form, their passports/ID proofs and parental authorization form must be identical. Mismatch of signatures will result in delay in processing the OCI application, which is also liable to be rejected. (Click here for the format). Note: One parent may sign the Parental Authorization Form only in the following conditions:
• If parents are divorced and only one parent has legal custody of the minor applicant (and the other parent has no visitation rights or paying child support), court order regarding the legal custody must be provided. If the court order is in any foreign language other than English, translation in English by authorized translator is to be enclosed.
• If one parent is not alive, copy of the death certificate must be provided.
• If the parent is single adoptive parent, copy of adoption document must be provided. 2

• Copy of the Indian passport of the Indian spouse or passport & OCI card (if Indian spouse holds OCI card) shall also be uploaded.

1. Poor quality of uploaded photo / signature. Please ensure to upload good quality photo and signature as per prescribed specifications.

oci.title: OCI re-issuance clarification
oci.chunk_text:
OCI Reissuance Clarification > OCI Card Reissue Guidelines

According to the recent relaxation in requirements for OCI Card Reissue:
(i) OCI cardholder is required to upload ONLINE a copy of the new passport and a recent photo (not more than 30 days old) each time a new passport is issued.  The uploading of these documents may be done within three months of receipt of the new passport.
[Please visit https://ociservices.gov.in/welcome and select the option ‘ OCI Miscellaneous Services’ for uploading copy of the passport, recent photograph and other documents. This does not involve any submission of documents through the Outsourcing Service Provider/Consulate and will be free of cost] .
(ii) However, the only exception to the above is mandatory re-issue of the OCI card when an applicant gets a new passport issued after completing 20 years of age. Please refer to https://services.vfsglobal.com/usa/en/ind/apply-oci-services for the process. The fees for this is US$ 25 and US$ 3 for Indian Community Welfare Fund (ICWF). Applicant also need to pay the Outsourcing Agency as service charge, and a fee for any optional services like shipping labels etc.
(iii) Foreign spouse of an Indian Citizen or spouse of an OCI cardholder is required to upload a copy of the new passport and a recent photo ONLINE each time a new passport is issued, along with a declaration on subsisting of marriage, copy of the Indian passport of the Indian spouse/passport and OCI card of the OCI cardholder spouse.
[Please visit https://ociservices.gov.in/welcome and select the option ‘ OCI Miscellaneous Services’ for uploading copy of the passport, recent photograph and other documents. This does not involve any submission of documents through the Outsourcing Service Provider/Consulate and will be free of cost] .

Eligibility for registration as OCI Cardholder: Following categories of foreign nationals are eligible for registration as Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) Cardholder: Any person of full age and capacity: who is a citizen of another country, but was a citizen of India at the time of, or at any time after the commencement of the Constitution i.e. 26.01.1950; or who is a citizen of another country, but was eligible to become a citizen of India at the time of the commencement of the Constitution i.e. on 26.01.1950; or who is a citizen of another country, but belonged to a territory that became part of India after 15.08.1947; or who is a child or a grandchild or a great grandchild of such a citizen; A person, who is a minor child of a person mentioned in (a) above; A person, who is a minor child, and whose both parents are citizens of India or one of the parents is a citizen of India; Spouse of foreign origin of a citizen of India or spouse of foreign origin of an Overseas Citizen of India Cardholder registered under section 7A of the Citizenship Act, 1955 and whose marriage has been registered and subsisted for a continuous period of not less than two years immediately preceding the presentation of the application. Following categories of foreign nationals are NOT eligible for registration as Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) Cardholder: Who or either of whose parents or grandparents or great grandparents is or had been a citizen of Pakistan, Bangladesh or such other country as the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, specify. oci.title: OCI re-issue on change of passport
oci.chunk_text:
Consulate General of India > Requirement of new OCI card in case of change of Passport

PRESS RELEASE
Requirement  of new OCI card in case of change of Passport
Overseas  Citizen of India card holders may please ensure following criteria of validity  of their OCI cards before planning their visit to India:
• Up to the age of 20  years, OCI card holder needs to get his/her OCI card reissued each time when  his/her passport is reissued.
• Between 21 and 50  years, reissue of OCI card is not mandatory when passport is reissued but  he/she has to carry old passport on which OCI card was issued along with the  current passport.
• After completion of 50  years of age, the OCI card is required to be reissued only once on renewal of passport. It is also  advised that while traveling one must always carry the expired passport (which  is endorsed on the valid OCI card) along with the OCI card and the current  passport.
Atlanta
07 Nov 2019

way of naturalization/registration: > ADULT (Applicants of or above the age of 18 years):

S. No. Document
1. Duly signed OCI Application Form in original. The application may be submitted online on the Government of India’s official website https://ociservices.gov.in/ and physical copy of the OCI application needs to be submitted with supporting documents. Please read the following carefully:
• If you are applying for OCI card for the first time and you never held PIO card, kindly apply for new OCI registration.
• If you are already an OCI Cardholder, kindly use OCI Miscellaneous Services.
• If you are a PIO Cardholder, kindly register through OCI Registration (In Lieu Of Valid PIO-Card).
• If you are a PIO Cardholder and card is in lost state, kindly register through OCI Registration (In Lieu Of Lost PIO -Card).
• To reprint your already registered application, kindly use 'Re -Print Submitted Application' service. In case of urgent travel, applicants may apply for appropriate visa.
2. Photograph & Signature: For detailed specifications - please click here
• The physical photo must be affixed on the physical application form and the digital photo must be uploaded on the OCI form online. Physical and uploaded photograph must be identical.
• The digital signature must also be uploaded online on the OCI portal (only in blue or black ink). Uploaded signature must match with the signature on the physical application form and passport.
3. Copy of current valid passport with validity of minimum 6 months at the time of submission of application. Information page of the passport should be duly signed at the designated The document must be self-attested. space.

oci.chunk_text:
way of naturalization/registration: > ADULT (Applicants of or above the age of 18 years):

4. Copy of last held Indian passport (first 2 and last 2 pages). If copy of Indian passport is not available, copies of the documents submitted for obtaining Surrender Certificate. The document must be self-attested. 1
5. Copy of Naturalization Certificate (the docum ent must be self -attested). : The naturalization certificate should be duly signed at the designated space. If the applicant has acquired naturalization through parents and the applicant doesn’t possess separate naturalization certificate, a notarized affidavit signed by both parents may be submitted along with copies of their naturalization certificates (Click here for the formant) .
6. Copy of Surrender Certificate ( The docum ent must be self- attested). Note: This only applies to applicants who were naturalized from year 2010 onwards.
7. PROOF OF LEGAL STATUS IN THE USA (IF HOLDING NON-USA PASSPORT) (The docum ent must be self-attested). Please submit any one of the following documents:
• Copy of valid Green Card – Front and Back, OR
• Copy of valid EAD – Front and Back, OR
• Copy of valid long-term US visa, OR
• In case visa extension is pending, I-797A Approval Notice / I-797C Receipt Notice along with recently expired visa may be submitted.
8. Proof of Marital Status (Married /Divo rced/W ido w ) (The docum e nt must be self - attested)
• Copy of the marriage certificate, if married.
• Copy of the divorce decree, if divorced. If re -married, include a copy of the marriage certificate.
• Copy of the Death certificate, if spouse is deceased.

way of naturalization/registration: > ADULT (Applicants of or above the age of 18 years):

• If proof of marital status is not available, a notarized affidavit may be submitted, thereby confirming the marital status and indicating the reasons for non - availability of requisite certificate. Note: If a marriage certificate or death certificate was issued by a foreign authority, it must be apostilled or attested by the concerned foreign Mission. Please do not send original apostilled documents to VFS office. We required self-attested copies of apostilled documents. 2

oci.chunk_text:
way of naturalization/registration: > ADULT (Applicants of or above the age of 18 years):

9. Name Change Document issued by the local court or a duly notarized affidavit regarding change in name, if the current legal name as per current foreign passport is different from the name given in the last held Indian passport. Previous name as per last held Indian passpor t must invariably be mentioned in the OCI application, failing which the OCI application is liable to be rejected. To be more specific, previous name must be mentioned even in case of minor variation, including variation of a single letter. The following e xamples may help: Example 1: If a person’s name as per last held Indian passport is TRIPTA TIWARI and the name as per foreign passport is TRIPTA TYAGI (surname changed after marriage), previous name as per last held Indian passport must be mentioned as TRIPTA TIWARI in the relevant column of the online OCI application. Example 2: If a person’s name as per last held Indian passport is HARISH CHANDER GUPTA and the name as per foreign passport is HARISH C. GUPTA, previous name as per last held Indian passport must be mentioned as HARISH CHANDER GUPTA in the relevant column of the online OCI application. Example 3: If a person’s name as per last held Indian passport is GIRDHAR PRAKASH and the name as per foreign passport is GIRI DHAR PRAKASH (one more ‘i ’ in the first name), previous name as per last held Indian passport must be mentioned as GIRDHAR PRAKASH in the relevant column of the online OCI application. Example 4: If a person’s name as per last held Indian passport is CHARU LATA and the name as per foreign passport is LATA CHARU, previous name as per last held Indian passport must be mentione d as CHARU LATA in the relevant column of the online OCI application. Example 5: If a person’s name as per last held Indian passport is GHANSHYAMBHAI PATEL and the name as per foreign passport is GHANSHYAM PATEL, previous name as per last held Indian passport must be mentioned as GHANSHYAMBHAI PATEL in the relevant column of the online OCI application. Note : Date of birth in the current foreign passport must match with the date of birth mentioned in the last held Indian passport. Mismatch is not acceptable and the application is liable to be rejected. 3

oci.chunk_text:
way of naturalization/registration: > ADULT (Applicants of or above the age of 18 years):

10. Copy of Employment / Work Letter (the docu m ent must be self-attested) :
• If applicant is employed, a letter from the employer describing job profile of the applicant may be provided.
• If applicant is self-employed / doing business, some documentary proof of self-employment/business may be provided.
• If applicant is retired, some documentary proof regarding retirement and details of the last employer may be provided.
• If applicant is a student, some documentary proof, e. g. admission letter, may be provided.
• If applicant has never been employed/self-employed, a written statement may be submitted.
11. Copies of OCI cards issued to parents and spouse, if ever obtained and availab le (The document must be self-attested).
12. Copy of Indian visa, if ever obtained and available (The document must be self- attested).
13. Proof of address (The document must be self-attested) : Proof of address must match with the present address as per application. Copy of any one of the following documents may be provided as proof of address:
• State issued Identity Card, OR
• Driving license, OR
• Utility bill – water / gas / electricity / telephone (Latest one, not more than 3 month old), OR
• Valid Lease Agreement, OR
• Mortgage, OR
• Income Tax Return, OR
• For college/university students living in university housing/dormitories, a letter from the institution on official letterhead giving details of the applicant’s present address, OR
• In case of applicant residing with parents / children / relatives, a notarized undertaking from them with any copy of address proof as indicated above. Note:
• Expired documents like lease/driving license are not acceptable as valid proof of address.

oci.chunk_text:
way of naturalization/registration: > ADULT (Applicants of or above the age of 18 years):

• PO Box number is not acceptable as valid proof of address.
• Copy of Driver’s License should not be cut down to smaller size. 4
14. Proof of native address for non -US nationals living in the USA (The docum ent must be self- attested) : Non-US nationals residing in the USA on a valid long -term visa should submit address proof of their home country. In the absence of address proof, a notarized statement must be provided giving details of native address. Applicants having dual nationality should submit proofs of native address of both the countries. IMPORTANT NOTE: If any supporting document is in a foreign language other than English, it should be translated in English by authorized translator.
15. Affidavit in lieu of originals: A notarized affidavit needs to be submitted that the documents in support of the OCI application are true copies of the original documents, where only copies are being provided (- please click here) .
16. Undertaking by the OCI applicant (please click here) .
17. Consent Letter, authorizing Indian Embassy/Consulate to make necessary corrections on observing errors in the OCI application (- please click here) . Note: Consent letter is just for the sake of facilitating an OCI applicant to avoid delay in processing the OCI application and it is not an assurance to edit the OCI application completely. The responsibility lies primarily with the applicant to fill in correct details in the OCI application. Also that some details as per the OCI application are not editable subsequently. In some cases, the OCI application with errors is liable to be rejected and may be returned to the applicant for submitting fresh OCI application with correct details.

• Application confirmation letter/payment confirmation is mandatory. Complete the process online on VFS India Consular Application Centre’s website to get the application confirmation letter/payment confirmation.
• Don’t forget to enclose the application confirmation receipt. If paying by Money Order or Banker’s Check, it should be made in favor of “VFS Services (USA) Inc.” PERSONAL CHECKS ARE NOT ACCEPTABLE. Please ensure to update the correct details of the instrument (Money Order / Banker’s Check).

• To complete registration on VFS Portal, (Please click here) . 5
ADDITIONAL IMPORTANT INFORMATION Documents in support of the OCI application must be uploaded onl ine. The supporting documents (maximum size 1000kb) to be uploaded broadly fall under the following categories:

2. All the supporting documents, including those which may not be uploaded under broad categories, must be submitted with the application form as per the checklist.
3. Indian Embassy / Consulate reserves the right to ask for additional documents for processing the OCI application. Embassy/Consulate is under no obligation to inform reasons, if the OCI application is rejected and the decision of the Embassy/Consulate wi ll be final. COMMON MISTAKES IN OCI APPLICATIONS RESULTING IN REJECTION
1. Poor quality of uploaded photo / signature. Please ensure to upload good quality photo and signature as per prescribed specifications. 6
2. All supporting documents not uploaded online.
3. Incorrect passport number / date of issue of passport
4. Incorrect name / place of birth / date of birth
5. Full names of parents / spouse not mentioned or not matching with their current legal names.
6. Marital status / spouse name not mentioned.
7. Incorrect contact numbers and email address.
8. Part-B of OCI application not signed / Part-B (Minor Child) not signed by any of the parents
9. Previous name not mentioned (if there is change of name, kindly mention the same in relevant column of the application and provide supporting documents).

11. Proof of native address not provided (proof of native address must be provided if application is being submitted in a country of residence other than home country). USEFUL TIPS FOR FILLING OCI APPLICATION ONLINE
1. Please ensure that you have all the supporting documents in pdf and photo/signature in JPEG format as per specifications before starting online application.
2. Fill all the details in the application very carefully and exactly as per documents. Please ensure that all the details like full names, date of birth, place of birth are exactly as per current passport. Please note that the date of birth, if different from the one mentioned in the last held Indian passport, is not acceptable.
3. Upload all the supporting documents under their correct category / equivalent category (e.g. Birth Certificate can be uploaded under Relationship category). If you are unable to find suitable category to upload the document, please upload all the remaining documents (including any legal document) under current passport category along with current passport. MOST IMPORTANT IS TO UPLOAD ALL THE SUPPORTING DOCUMENTS.
4. Kindly check all the details of the OCI application once printed. In case photo/signature and documents are not uploaded properly, these can be uploaded easily by selecting appropriate option (Re -upload image/upload/re - upload documents) available on the website. Please note that the file reference number required to re -upload photo/signature/documents is written vertically on left side and also below the bar code at the bottom of first page of 7
application form submitted online.
5. In case any information is wrong, please fill the form again. 8

Miscellaneous FAQs

OCI Miscellaneous Services are regarding updating of following details and re-issuance of OCI Cards which can be availed of only by the registered OCI Cardholders.
• Issuance of new passport after completing 20 years of age;

surrender_renunciation.title: Renunciation service overview
surrender_renunciation.chunk_text:
Surrender of Indian passport > Surrender of Indian passport

• Overview Surrender and Renunciation of Indian Citizenship applies only to applicants of Indian Origin. Under The Indian Citizenship Act, 1955, Persons of Indian Origin is not allowed DUAL Citizenship. If a person has ever held an Indian Passport and has obtained the Passport of another
                                                                        country, they will be required to surrender their Indian Passport immediately after gaining another Country’s nationality. If a person has ever held an Indian passport and has obtained the passport of another country, they will be required to surrender their Indian passport immediately after gaining another
                                                                        country's nationality. After Renunciation of Indian Citizenship, it is necessary to apply for Surrender or a Renunciation certificate. A stamp saying "cancelled due to acquiring foreign nationality" is required. It should be noted that Indian passports that carry only a "cancelled stamp" are not considered renounced
                                                                        of their Indian citizenship. While applying for consular services Visa or OCI, it is mandatory to provide proof of your cancelled Indian passport. If such evidence cannot be provided, applicants will be required
                                                                        to obtain a renunciation certificate. While applying for Renunciation of Indian Citizenship, there are many procedures that must be followed, including the submission of the duly filled application form as well as current
                                                                        photographs and relevant documents. While enquiring about the fees that are levied for the relevant stamps and certificates, it is also essential to identify your area of jurisdiction
                                                                        and service centers. It is not necessary for travellers to carry a Certificate of Renunciation of Indian Citizenship during their travel to India. It should be noted that it is illegal to continue to use an Indian passport after the renunciation of Indian citizenship and defaulters will be faced with penalties. Guidelines for Shipping Service & its packaging Third Party Offered Courier Service - points to note You can purchase third party offered courier service. Please enclose only one application per package. Don’t enclose multiple applications in the same package. Your return shipping address must match with the proof of address submitted as part of your application. VFS won't be responsible for any delays or damages if packages are in transit for inbound or outbound couriers. Return address on the shipping label must match the address on the application form. Do not provide shipping address of Courier stores or Hold at Location stations. We don’t accept USPS pre-paid labels having expiry date limitation. You are responsible for tracking your package and schedule a pick up from the VFS Consular application Centre once ready. VFS won't be responsible for any delays or damages if packages are in transit for inbound or outbound couriers. Policy - Return of incomplete documents after 20 days. Incomplete application: If the application is not completed within 20 calendar days, then VFS will return your application unprocessed. In this scenario, the Consular and ICWF fee will be refunded post deduction of applicable postal charges (if applicable). Photocopy documents received after 20 days will be shredded and originals if any received will be returned to the Embassy of India or Consulate General of India. Applicants should contact the Embassy of India or Consulate General of India directly to receive their original documents, once VFS returns the original documents to the Embassy of India or Consulate General of India. In this scenario, only the Consular and ICWF fee will be refunded post deduction of applicable postal charges (if applies). Policy – Additional documents after 07 days. Additional documents: If the additional documents are not completed within 07 calendar days then Embassy/Consulates may stop processing your application. In
                                                                                            this scenario, no fees will be refunded.

• Overview General instructions for Miscellaneous Services Applicants, while submitting applications for all kinds of consular services may submit only notarized copies of Passport and address proof. No originals are required to be submitted. However, for death documentation the passport in original of the dead person must be presented. The rest of the directions may please be seen in the relevant links of the respective services. The Embassy / Consulates reserves the right to reject attestation of documents, the contents of which are objectionable or contrary to the Rules. "Please note No Commercial Documents are attested by the Embassy / Consulates. The same should be apostilled from US Government Authorities for presenting in India." Apostille Convention: The Hague Convention, to which India and USA are signatories, abolishes the requirement of legalization for Foreign Public Documents. With the certification by the Hague Convention 'Apostille', the document is entitled to recognition in India and vice versa and no certification by the Embassy of India is required. The Convention applies to public documents which have been executed in the territory of one Contracting State and which have to be produced in the territory of another Contracting State. The Embassy / Consulates does not attest any document issued by authorities in India. If any document issued by authorities in India such as birth and death certificates, affidavits, educational documents/diplomas, marriage certificate, Driving License etc. are required to be presented to authorities in USA, those should be apostilled in India. For details, please check the website “Legalization of Documents” at http://www.mea.gov.in/apostille.htm . It is mandatory for the documents issued by the US Government authorities to be apostilled by the relevant authorities in the USA before presenting the document for attestation at the Embassy / Consulates. Note: Embassy / Consulates would continue to offer services like death certificates, life certificates directly to the applicants as per extant practice. However, in case the applicants wish to avail these services from VFS Global, they can avail the same as any other miscellaneous consular service from VFS Global on payment of the applicable service fee. Please refer to the directions provided in the checklist as available in the

• Overview NORI waiver certificate is issued to Indian nationals to waive off two years of home (India) residency which is mandatory for all J-1 visa holders, as per US Immigration Laws, who wishes to apply for H1B Visa (Work Visas). NORI applicants staying in United States or any other country outside India are required to apply at the nearest Indian Mission/Post through VFS Global NORI applications for J-1 categories (Au pair and Edu Care, Camp Counselor, Intern, International Visitor (department of state use), Professor and Research Scholar, Short-term Scholar, Specialist, Student, college/university, student, secondary, Summer Work Travel, Teacher, Trainee) shall follow the following process:- The following documents are to be submitted along with an ink signed application requesting for issuance of NORI: Original notarized affidavit containing full details of his/her visit to USA on student visa, especially, details of his/her Indian passport number, date and place of issue, period of stay in USA, his/her address in USA during his/her stay there and his/her present address in India where he/she is currently staying; Original notarized bio-data containing full details of his/her educational qualifications, details of Passports/J1 Visa, his/her present address in India where he/she is currently staying, etc; Copies of the Indian passports including the one on which the candidate travelled to US and US J1 visa pages; Copy of Third Party Bar Code page from the US State Department containing the applicant’s Waiver Review Case File Number required to be quoted in the NORI Certificate (For Details, Please visit https://travel.state.gov/content/visas/en/study-exchange/student/residency-waiver.html). NORI applications for J-1 category of Government Visitor shall follow the above-mentioned process after seeking clearance from their parent department. NORI applications for J-1 category of Physician shall follow the following the above-mentioned process after obtaining necessary clearance from Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. Specimen copies of the bio-data and affidavit for Miscellaneous Services can be found in the fee and documents required section. General instructions for Miscellaneous Services Applicants, while submitting applications for all kinds of consular services may submit only notarized copies of Passport and address proof. No originals are required to be submitted. However, for death documentation the passport in original of the dead person must be presented. The rest of the directions may please be seen in the relevant links of the respective services. The Embassy / Consulates reserves the right to reject attestation of documents, the contents of which are objectionable or contrary to the Rules. "Please note No Commercial Documents are attested by the Embassy / Consulates. The same should be apostilled from US Government Authorities for presenting in India." Apostille Convention: The Hague Convention, to which India and USA are signatories, abolishes the requirement of legalization for Foreign Public Documents. With the certification by the Hague Convention 'Apostille', the document is entitled to recognition in India and vice versa and no certification by the Embassy of India is required. The Convention applies to public documents which have been executed in the territory of one Contracting State and which have to be produced in the territory of another Contracting State. The Embassy / Consulates does not attest any document issued by authorities in India. If any document issued by authorities in India such as birth and death certificates, affidavits, educational documents/diplomas, marriage certificate, Driving License etc. are required to be presented to authorities in USA, those should be apostilled in India. For details, please check the website “Legalization of Documents” at http://www.mea.gov.in/apostille.htm . It is mandatory for the documents issued by the US Government authorities to be apostilled by the relevant authorities in the USA before presenting the document for attestation at the Embassy / Consulates. Note: Embassy / Consulates would continue to offer services like death certificates, life certificates directly to the applicants as per extant practice. However, in case the applicants wish to avail these services from VFS Global, they can avail the same as any other miscellaneous consular service from VFS Global on payment of the applicable service fee. Consulate General of India > Attestation of Documents

Please send a prepaid return envelope of USD 20.00 along with your application
Walk-in consular services discontinued
ATTESTATION OF DOCUMENTS SUCH AS COPY OF INDIAN PASSPORT/OCI CARD, APPLICATION FOR PAN CARD, BANK STATEMENT, SALARY STATEMENT, COPY OF DOCUMENTS ISSUED BY US AUTHORITIES (US PASSPORT, DRIVING LICENCE, ETC) Applicants resident in Alabama, Florida, Georgia, Mississippi, Puerto Rico, South Carolina, Tennessee and US Virgin Islands can apply for attestation of documents at this Consulate.
Appostille Convention: The Hague Convention, to which India and USA are signatories, abolishes the requirement of legalization for Foreign Public Documents. With the certification by the Hague Convention 'Apostille', the document is entitled to recognition in India and vice versa and no certification by the Consulate is required . The Convention applies to public documents which have been executed in the territory of one Contracting State and which have to be produced in the territory of another Contracting State.
The Consulate does not attest any document issued by the authorities in India. If any document issued by authorities in India such as birth and death certificates, affidavits, educational documents/diplomas, marriage certificate, Driving License,etc, is required to be presented to authorities in USA, it should be apostilled in India. For details, please visit the website: http://www.mea.gov.in/apostille.htm .  However, for the ease of Indian nationals, the Consulate does “True Copy Attestation Only” of the documents issued by authorities in India, which does not mean certifying the genuineness of the document.

global_entry.title: Global Entry Programme
global_entry.chunk_text:
Consulate General of India > Global Entry Program (GEP) for Indian Nationals

Global Entry Program (GEP) of U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) for Indian Citizens
Global Entry is a U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) program, which allows expedited clearance for pre-approved, low-risk travelers upon arrival in the United States. Members enter the United States through automatic kiosks at select U.S. airports .
How to Apply for Global Entry:
Citizens of India are eligible for Global Entry. Applications must be submitted through US Customs and Border Protection(CBP)’s Trusted Traveler Programs (TTP) website as Step 1.
Application Process for Background Check for GEP:
1. Apply Online with US CBP: Apply and complete application process at TTP website: https://www.cbp. gov/travel/trusted-traveler- programs/global-entry of US CBP as Step 1.
2. For the applicant presently living in USA, after completion of Step ‘1’, he/she needs to submit the requisite information in the website of Global Passport Seva Project ( https://portal4. passportindia.gov.in/Online/ welcomeLink ) for completion of background check in India. After completion of online submission, he/she should submit the physical application at the VFS Global Application Centre, along with applicable fee, as per guidelines given on its website: https://visa. vfsglobal.com/usa/en/ind .

community_events.title: Know India Programme
community_events.chunk_text:
Consulate General of India > Know India Programme

Announcement of the 88th edition of the Know India Programme (KIP) for Young Professionals scheduled to be organized from 16-29 August 2026
KIP is a flagship programme of this Ministry of External Affairs that seeks to reconnect PIOs to their ethnic roots besides showcasing the rich cultural heritage of India and its recent spectacular developmental efforts. Ministry endeavors to present various facets of contemporary Indian Art, Heritage, Culture, Economy, Innovations, Start-ups, Science & Technology, etc., to the youth members of the Indian Diaspora and strives to motivate and inspire them to contribute and participate in the transformative initiatives of the Government of India as part of its march towards Viksit Bharat. Since its inception in 2003-04, Ministry has successfully organized 83 editions of the KIP with participation of more than 3000 youth PIO members.
Ministry proposes to organize the 88th edition of the Know India Programme, from 16 to 29 August 2026 for 'Young Professionals' in the 24–28 years age group. Under this edition, 25 youth members of the Indian diaspora, including PIOs, OCIs and NRIs, will be invited to visit India for a two-week Programme.
i. The eligibility age criteria for participants was revised from 21–35 years to 18–28 years, with participants divided into two cohorts: 18–23 years (Scholars and Innovators) and 24–28 years (Young Professionals).
ii. Separate editions of the Programme would be organized for the two cohorts, with each edition comprising of 25 participants.
iii. The duration of each Programme will be two weeks, inclusive of travel time.

community_events.title: Know India Programme
community_events.chunk_text:
Consulate General of India > Know India Programme

iv. The Programme would be open to youth of Indian origin, including Persons of Indian Origin (PIOs), Overseas Citizens of India (OCIs), as well as for Non-Resident Indians (NRIs).
Interested participants may send their applications (in MS Word format), along with Educational Qualification Certificate, Passport, Passport sized colored photograph, PIO/OCI Carddocuments related to to the Consulate General of India in Atlanta at hoc.atlanta@mea.gov.in latest by July 16, 2026.

community_events.title: Guidelines for Indian students in the USA
community_events.chunk_text: Consulate General of India Atlanta *** Guidelines for Indian Students in the United States Before you arrive  Credentials of Universities: Perform due diligence and thoroughly check the credentials of Universities / Institutions online and with peer groups before taking admission.  Travelling to the US: Do carry financial instruments sufficient to meet your needs while travel- ing to the United States. Carry proofs of payment of university fees and tuition deposit (if any) along with confirmation of accommodation before entering the country. After reaching in the US  Student registration: Indian students are advised to register in the Consulate website at https://indiainatlanta.gov.in/eoial_pages/MjQ2 for close engagement with Consulate.  Know the University/Institution: Know various services offered by your university and avail them. Generally, most of these services are funded from tuition fees. Enquire about them at the International Student Services Office.  Know your surroundings: It is important to know and avoid neighborhoods that are not well-lit and places that are known locally as ‘shady’. Do not venture out late at night to such areas. Move around in groups or at least with a few friends, if you must.  Remain connected: Be in touch with the Consulate, local mentors/guardians and Indian com- munity organizations. Update your whereabouts with family and close friends especially when moving outside alone.  Abide by local law: Take general precautions and abide by local laws and regulations including while driving or undertaking recreational activities (For example – wearing seatbelts even if sit- ting in the rear; not driving/swimming in inebriated condition; using life jackets during boating; dressing adequately to avoid hypothermia etc.) Avoid substance abuse.  Seek help if depressed/anxious: It is natural to feel lonely, while being in a new environment, away from home. Share your feelings with family, fellow students and teachers and feel free to connect with the Consulate. Do not hesitate to call professional help or seek university services if you are feeling depressed or having anxiety attack.  Medical insurance: Make sure you have valid and adequate medical insurance during your stay in the United States, preferably as recommended by the University.  Keep your Personal Information and Documents Safe: Keep your personal details safe, including your bank account and credit card details, since they can be easily misused. Be very careful about storage of documents such as passport/visa, identification, immigration forms etc.  Beware of Money Mules: Anyone can be approached by money mules but criminals often target students. Beware of such people, social networking scams, and telephone calls requesting for your personal information and/or bank account details for money transfer Working in the US  Work authorization: Engage only in jobs that comply with your visa status. Permissions required may be obtained in advance from appropriate authorities before engaging in any type of internship/employment. Some information in this context could be found here (hyper link

training). Avoid working in unsafe environments. In case of Emergency while in the US  US Authorities: Dial 911 immediately. In case of any untoward incident, report to the administrative division and International Students Office at the University immediately.  Consulate: Please note the Consulate’s emergency number +1 404 910 7919. For routine queries, please call +1 404 963-5902. In case of any difficulty, please reach out to the following points of contact at the Embassy: Ms. Nishi Arora, Consul (HOC): hoc.atlanta@mea.gov.in Mr. Ajay Singh, ASO (Passport): passport.atlanta@mea.gov.in *******

Bi-weekly Open House at the Consulate General of India, Atlanta
We are pleased to announce that the Consulate General of India, Atlanta will be holding bi-weekly OPEN HOUSE from 1100-1200 hrs (ET) on every first (01 st ) and thirds (03 rd ) Thursdays at the Consulate at 5549, Glenridge Dr, Atlanta, GA-30342. The first Open House will be held on March 20, 2025.
All the applicants of Passport, Visa, OCI and other Consular Services and Indian nationals including Students who wish to seek guidance or resolution of any grievance can come and do so. Applicants are advised to bring all relevant documents with them in order to get proper rederessal of their grievances.
Note: If the Consul General is out of office, other officers in the Consulate will be available to meet and provide information.

community_events.title: Study in India programme
community_events.chunk_text:
Consulate General of India > Study in India (SII) Programme

The Study in India (SII) program is a flagship project of Ministry of Education (MoE), Government of India to encourage international students to explore educational opportunities at top Indian universities. The SII program has constructed a seamless system for students to register for the program and explore courses across prestigious Indian institutes. Concomitantly, SII portal ( https://studyinindia.gov.in/ ) , a key initiative aimed at promoting India as a global destination for higher education was jointly launched on 3rd August 2023 by the Ministry of Education (MoE), Ministry of External Affairs (MEA), and Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA). 2. The Indian Education system is the world's second largest Higher Education System with more than 800 universities, 39,000 colleges and an enrolling capacity of 20 million students. Higher Education Institutions in India offer courses/degrees that are competitive in the world market in terms of quality but are delivered at one fourth the cost, hence guaranteeing value-for-money education. 3. The SII portal is a one-stop platform that facilitates admission procedures, course applications, and visa formalities for international students wishing to pursue undergraduate, postgraduate, short-term, or research-based academic programs in India. It serves as a seamless digital gateway to India’s higher education ecosystem. All foreign students who wish to study in India are required to register on the SII portal and submit the required information. Upon successful registration, a unique ID (SII-ID) is generated. This ID is mandatory for applying for an Indian student visa (e-Student Visa) through the Indian Visa Portal. For more information, please visit: https://www.studyinindia.gov. in/

Consulate General of India > Official App Indian Visa Su-Swagatam

Consulate General of India Atlanta Official App Indian Visa Su-Swagatam
Government of India has launched “ Official App Indian Visa Su-Swagatam ” Mobile App to facilitate travel to India. Through this App (available on Google Play store for Android users and on App store for IOS users), visitors would be facilitated with following visa related services:-
a) Apply for visa – (Regular Visa, e-Visa, Visa on arrival)
b) Online Foreigners Regional Registration Office (e-FRRO) services-Apply e-FRRO Services (like visa extension, visa conversion, exit-permit etc. in India).
c) Check Status- (i) Status of visa application
(ii) Status of e-FRRO applications.
d) Notification – Advisories/notifications by Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) and Bureau of Immigration (BoI).
e) Language Assistance-Signage and Language converter (multi languages)
f) Chatbot- Help center for Applicant queries.
g) Nearby places- Foreigners would be facilitated in exploring nearby places like Tourist Places, Govt. Agencies, transport services, Entertainment, health services, Religious places, Lodging, Boarding facilities, etc.
h) Useful Links:
(i) Medical Emergency- Ntional Accreditation Board for Hospitals & Healthcare Providers (NABH) accredited hospitals by Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoH&FEW).
(ii) Business in India- Make in India portal of Government of India.
(iii) Foreigners Safety- Ministry of Tourism Portal for all emergency and contacts helpline.
(iv) Tourism- Incredible India Portal of Ministry of Tourism to explore tourism places in India.
(v) Yoga and Spirituality- Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoH&FW)portal to get authentic institutes for practicing Yoga in India.

fraud_advisory.title: Advisory on fraudulent callers
fraud_advisory.chunk_text:
Consulate General of India

It has been brought to the notice of the Consulate that some fraudsters
                    are
                    spoofing telephone lines of Embassy and Consulates to make calls aimed at cheating people. Some of
                    these
                    calls are shown as being from the Embassy telephone numbers ( 202-939-7000 ), Consulate General of India, Atlanta’s telephone number
                    ( 404-963-5902 ) while
                    others simply use
                    Embassy/Consulate identity. These fraudsters either seek personal information like credit card
                    details
                    etc. or try to extort money from Indian nationals by inter alia claiming
                    that
                    there are errors in their passports, visa forms, immigration forms etc. which could be rectified by
                    paying money, and at the same time warning that the so called errors, if not rectified, could result
                    in
                    deportation of the individual to India or their imprisonment in USA. In some cases, these fraudsters
                    have also falsely claimed that they received such privileged information from the Embassy or other
                    authorities in India. Visa applicants have also received such calls purporting to be from the
                    Embassy/Consulate.
